overview: Geto’s settings control when and where his summons appear and how his staged projectile volley fires.
technicalOverview: Suguru Geto (CP_120) uses UCP_120_ActionController and the CP_120 AI think node. CharacterUniqueDataTable4 stores a block of tuning floats per mechanic: the normal-attack rows place and time shikigami 0/1/4/5 or a third effect, the cursed-energy rows place shikigami 2/3 or drive a staged projectile volley, and the base CP_120 row is all zeros. The runtime does not look up these rows by name in action code: AGameCharacter builds UniqueRows in Id_CharacterUnique order, so zero-based row index 1 means ATTACKA, 2 means ATTACKB, 3 means ATTACKC, 4 means ATTACKD, 5 means ATTACKF, 6 means ATTACKG and 7 means ATTACKH. FGameCharacterAction::GetOwnerUniqueFloat(ValueIndex, RowIndex) then reads UniqueRows[RowIndex]->FloatValue[ValueIndex] with no bounds check. Ground and air action twins use the same row. Effects below are traced from reconstructed source; where a generic helper could read a row but no CP_120 call was found, it is left unresolved instead of claimed as a setting.

CP_120.title: All-zero base row
CP_120.overview: This is row 0 of Id_CharacterUnique and every float is zero. No CP_120-specific action body in the traced source indexes row 0. Generic helpers can read row 0 of any character, but the CP_120 call sites found all use rows 1-7, so no runtime meaning is assigned to these zeros.

0.label: Generic turn / fallback time value
0.simple: No CP_120-specific visible change was traced for this zero.
0.technical: Generic readers exist: SteerTowardSecondaryTarget divides the unsigned horizontal angle by GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(0,0) and calls RotateTowardLocation with that time, but its traced callers are CN_041, CN_140 and CP_060 actions, not CP_120. Projection-sorcery restraint also uses column 0 as a restraint-time fallback only when the damage row is missing; MakeUniqueCameraRequest would use it as camera X only if called. No such CP_120 call was found.

1.label: Generic AI hold / camera Y value
1.simple: No CP_120-specific visible change was traced for this zero.
1.technical: CursedEnergyAttack1Hold::Reset computes Duration = F(1,0) * CursedEnergyLevel + F(0,0), and MakeUniqueCameraRequest reads column 1 as camera Y. The hold executor is explicitly built by CP_040 behavior code; no CP_120 registration or camera-request call was found in the traced Source.

2.label: Generic AI hold / camera Z value
2.simple: No CP_120-specific visible change was traced for this zero.
2.technical: CursedEnergyAttack2Hold::Reset computes Duration = F(2,0) * CursedEnergyLevel + F(0,0), and MakeUniqueCameraRequest reads column 2 as camera Z. CP_050 registers a different 2-hold executor; no CP_120 registration or camera-request call was found.

notes.text: A zero value is not evidence that the slot is unused; these entries are unresolved because only generic, non-CP_120 call paths were found.
The exported character list has a trailing None after ATTACKH; AGameCharacter adds optional rows, so a missing row becomes a null UniqueRows entry. CP_120 code does not index that position.

CP_120_ATTACKA.title: NormalAttack_1 summon and third-shot tuning
CP_120_ATTACKA.overview: Row 1 shapes the first normal-attack group: two shikigami placed left and right, then a third start that creates an FX_CP_120_04101_1 fade effect at a collision-adjusted point.

0.label: Shikigami attack time
0.simple: Sets the attack timing passed to both summoned shikigami.
0.technical: On G1 start counts 0 and 1, FShikigamiDamageActionParam.Value64 is assigned F(0,1) = 0.6 before ChangeAction(Attack_1). The request header documents Value64 as a time; the CP_120 body forwards it without further arithmetic.

1.label: Shikigami side distance
1.simple: Controls how far the two shikigami stand to either side of Geto.
1.technical: Candidate local Y offset = positive F(1,1) = 90. Start count 0 negates it (-90, left), start count 1 keeps it (+90, right). StateCondition_ClampLocalOffset traces around the candidate with extent (50,50,0), possibly moving it before it is rotated into world space as F*X + R*Y + U*Z.

2.label: Shikigami aim pitch limit (degrees)
2.simple: Limits how high or low the summoned shikigami aims.
2.technical: On both summon starts this is passed as MaxPitch and MaxDown to CN122_AimRotation: FMath::Clamp elevation to [-30, 30] degrees when the helper reports a positive pitch sign, and to the mirrored interval for the negative sign. FMath::Clamp boundaries are inclusive.

3.label: Shikigami aim yaw limit (degrees)
3.simple: Effectively prevents the summoned shikigami from turning sideways.
3.technical: Passed as MaxYaw = F(3,1) = 0. CN122_AimRotation takes FMath::Min(angle, 0) for a nonnegative angle and uses 0 for a negative angle, so the resulting yaw is 0 degrees.

4.label: Maximum target elevation (degrees)
4.simple: Caps how far above or below Geto the third-shot aim point may sit.
4.technical: On G1 start count 2, raw clamped elevation is compared with abs(F(4,1)) = 30 degrees. Only when abs(elevation) > 30 does the code rotate the horizontal target vector about the right axis by 30 degrees (sign chosen from target Z) to rebuild the target Z; otherwise the original target is kept.

5.label: Maximum effect distance
5.simple: Keeps the third-shot aim point within a fixed distance of Geto.
5.technical: After elevation handling, if the delta from Geto to the target exceeds F(5,1) = 1800 world units, the target becomes owner location + delta.GetSafeNormal() * 1800. A delta equal to or below 1800 is unchanged.

6.label: Effect upward offset
6.simple: Raises the third-shot effect above the aim point.
6.technical: Added as owner up vector * F(6,1) = 220 world units to form the effect transform translation. The same offset vector is negated to build the transform X axis.

7.label: Effect forward offset
7.simple: Shifts the third-shot effect backward relative to Geto’s facing.
7.technical: Added as owner facing forward * F(7,1) = -50 world units. The negative value moves the effect opposite the facing direction; together with column 6 it forms Offset, and -Offset is used as the rotation X axis.

8.label: Summon height offset
8.simple: Helps choose a safe height for the first two shikigami.
8.technical: Candidate local Z offset = F(8,1) = 15 world units for both start count 0 and 1, passed to StateCondition_ClampLocalOffset before rotation into world space. The Z probe extent is 0 here, so only the forward and side traces can adjust the candidate.

9.label: Unresolved extra normal-attack value
9.simple: The export stores an extra number in this slot. Its effect is still unknown.
9.technical: The traced first-normal-attack effect placement reads row 1 slots 0 through 8 across its phases. Slot 9 is outside those reads. The negative export value alone gives no reliable unit or role.

notes.text: The two summon placements use different signs of the same side value: shikigami 0 is left, shikigami 1 is right.
Verification records confirm the retail association: column 2 is the aim pitch passed as MaxUp/MaxDown, column 3 is the yaw limit.
The first two starts use shikigami 0 and 1 and Attack_1; the third start makes an effect and a fade effect instead of another summon.

CP_120_ATTACKB.title: NormalAttack_1_1 shikigami placement
CP_120_ATTACKB.overview: Row 2 controls the single shikigami 4 summoned by the 1_1 normal-attack group, including its local placement, aim limits and Attack_5 timing.

0.label: Shikigami attack time
0.simple: Sets the attack timing for shikigami 4.
0.technical: F(0,2) = 1.0 is written to FShikigamiDamageActionParam.Value64 before ChangeAction(Attack_5). Value64 is documented as a time in the request struct; no CP_120 arithmetic is applied.

1.label: Local forward offset
1.simple: Places the summon slightly behind Geto along the facing axis.
1.technical: Candidate local X = F(1,2) = -20 world units. It is passed with Y and Z to StateCondition_ClampLocalOffset, which traces clearance with extent (50,50,0) before the offset is rotated into world space.

2.label: Local right offset
2.simple: Places the summon to Geto’s right.
2.technical: Candidate local Y = F(2,2) = 70 world units, processed by the same collision-adjusted local-offset path as columns 1 and 3.

3.label: Local up offset
3.technical: Candidate local Z = F(3,2) = 95 world units. With Z extent 0, the third probe leg is skipped and only X/Y obstacle traces can change the candidate.

4.label: Shikigami aim pitch limit (degrees)
4.simple: Limits how high or low the summon aims.
4.technical: Passed as MaxPitch and MaxDown to CN122_AimRotation with value 20 degrees, so elevation is clamped inclusively to the appropriate [-20, 20] signed interval.

5.label: Shikigami aim yaw limit (degrees)
5.simple: Limits sideways turning when the summon aims.
5.technical: Passed as MaxYaw = F(5,2) = 20 degrees. Positive horizontal angles are capped at 20 degrees and mirrored by GameRotation_SideOf when the target is on the other side; negative horizontal angles produce yaw 0 in this helper.

notes.text: Verification records confirm the retail association: column 4 is pitch (MaxUp/MaxDown) and column 5 is yaw (MaxYaw).
After placement, FX_CP_120_00111 is played 25 units up and 50 units forward of the summon with scale 1.5; those numbers are constants, not values from this row.

CP_120_ATTACKC.title: NormalAttack_2 paired-shikigami and cross-attack tuning
CP_120_ATTACKC.overview: Row 3 sets the ground/air NormalAttack_2 pair: it places shikigami 0 and 1, aims a shared target, and records cross locations used by the second start.

0.label: First attack time
0.simple: Sets the attack timing for the initial shikigami 2 requests.
0.technical: F(0,3) = 0.6 is copied into Value64 on the Attack_2 requests issued to shikigami 0 and 1. Value64 is documented as a request time.

1.label: Side separation
1.simple: Controls how far left and right the two shikigami appear.
1.technical: F(1,3) = 60 is used as right-vector magnitude. Shikigami 0 starts at owner location - side; shikigami 1 starts at owner location + side.

2.label: Elevation limit (degrees)
2.simple: Caps the elevation of the shared aiming point.
2.technical: F(2,3) = 25 supplies both MaxElevation and MinElevation = -MaxElevation. GameAnimNotify_ClampedElevation at 90/90 is then clamped inclusively to [-25, 25] degrees before the forward vector is rotated to get the target point.

3.label: Aim distance
3.simple: Sets how far in front of Geto the shared aim point is placed.
3.technical: The elevation-rotated facing vector is multiplied by F(3,3) = 800 world units and added to the owner location.

4.label: Cross attack time
4.simple: Sets the attack timing for the later crossing attack.
4.technical: On start count 1, F(4,3) = 0.8 is written to Value64 on the Attack_3 requests for each non-releasing shikigami, together with the stored cross location and direction.

5.label: Cross-location distance
5.simple: Sets how far toward the target each crossing point is recorded.
5.technical: Cross locations are owner location + normalized direction to the shared target * F(5,3) = 300 world units, then adjusted by column 6.

6.label: Cross-location up shift
6.simple: Offsets the two recorded crossing points vertically in opposite directions.
6.technical: F(6,3) = -50 is multiplied by the aim quaternion up vector. Shikigami 0’s stored point subtracts it and shikigami 1’s adds it; the same value also lowers/raises their initial placement along that aim-up axis.

notes.text: The cross request is issued only on the second attack start and is skipped for a shikigami already performing a release action.
Columns 0 and 4 are separate timings: column 0 is used for the initial Attack_2 pair, column 4 for the later Attack_3 pair.

CP_120_ATTACKD.title: NormalAttack_2_1 third-shot placement and aim
CP_120_ATTACKD.overview: Row 4 tunes the extra shot created by the 2_1 normal-attack group: a local offset is collision-adjusted, then aimed at the secondary target.

0.label: Shot pitch limit (degrees)
0.simple: Limits how high or low the extra shot aims.
0.technical: F(0,4) = 30 is passed as MaxUp and MaxDown to CN122_AimRotation with MaxYaw = 0.0f, so yaw is forced to 0 and elevation is clamped inclusively to the appropriate signed [-30, 30] interval.

1.label: Local up offset
1.simple: Raises the candidate shot position above Geto.
1.technical: F(1,4) = 200 is the Z component of FVector(F(2,4), F(3,4), F(1,4)). It is collision-probed with extent Z = 100; on a qualifying hit the Z candidate is rewritten from the hit distance and that extent.

2.label: Local forward offset
2.simple: Moves the candidate shot position in front of Geto.
2.technical: F(2,4) = 80 is the X component of the local offset. StateCondition_ClampLocalOffset probes forward by X - 50 and can rewrite X from the first filtered hit distance.

3.label: Local right offset
3.simple: Moves the candidate shot position to Geto’s left.
3.technical: F(3,4) = -55 is the Y component. Because it is negative, StateCondition_ClampLocalOffset probes toward negative Y; on a qualifying hit, Y is reconstructed as extent - hit distance rather than hit distance - extent.

notes.text: The extents (50,50,100) are trace clearance distances, not numeric clamps on the raw row values.
The shot uses FX_CP_120_04101_2 with a sub effect via SpawnFadeEffect; the effect IDs and the +25/-50/1.5 constants elsewhere are not unique-row values.

CP_120_ATTACKF.title: NormalAttack_3_1 shikigami timing
CP_120_ATTACKF.overview: Row 5 has one traced setting: the attack timing on the shikigami 5 request made by the 3_1 normal-attack group.

0.label: Shikigami attack time
0.simple: Sets the attack timing for shikigami 5.
0.technical: F(0,5) = 0.45 is assigned to Value64 before ChangeAction(Attack_4). The summon itself stays at the saved summon location and faces opposite Geto’s forward; no other column of this row is read in the CP_120 bodies.

notes.text: The row name is F because the exported Id_CharacterUnique order skips an E entry; the runtime row index is still 5.

CP_120_ATTACKG.title: CursedEnergyAttack_1 summon and staged volley
CP_120_ATTACKG.overview: Row 6 drives CursedEnergyAttack_1/its air twin: it spawns shikigami 3 with target-aware aim and creates a multi-stage FX_CP_120_04101 volley with configurable origin, pitch, spacing, scale and lead.

0.label: Shikigami forward spawn distance
0.simple: Sets how far in front of Geto shikigami 3 starts.
0.technical: The spawn origin is owner location + facing forward * F(0,6) + world up * 100. With the stored value 0, the shikigami starts at the owner location plus the fixed 100-unit height. The default target is one unit in front of that origin, replaced by the secondary target’s actor location when valid.

1.label: Fallback aim pitch limit (degrees)
1.simple: Limits vertical aim when the target was not down or blown away.
1.technical: The target-down/blown condition is captured in StartAttackHoming. If it was false, F(1,6) = 20 is passed as MaxPitch and MaxDown to CN122_AimRotation. If it was true, the code substitutes fixed 90/90 instead of reading this value.

2.label: Fallback aim yaw limit (degrees)
2.simple: Limits sideways aim when the target was not down or blown away.
2.technical: Used only in the same non-condition branch: MaxYaw = F(2,6) = 20 degrees. In the down/blown branch MaxYaw is fixed at 90 instead.

3.label: Projectile pitch limit (degrees)
3.simple: Limits vertical aim of the queued shot request.
3.technical: F(3,6) = 30 is passed as both MaxUp and MaxDown to CN122_AimRotation for the shot transform, with MaxYaw fixed at 0.0f. The request is queued only for UniqueAction parameter 1 and only when the action controller casts to UCP_120_ActionController.

4.label: Projectile origin height
4.simple: Raises the projectile volley above Geto.
4.technical: F(4,6) = 150 is multiplied by the owner up vector when building ShotRequest.Transform translation, in addition to owner forward * F(5,6) and the owner location.

5.label: Projectile origin distance
5.simple: Pushes the projectile volley in front of Geto.
5.technical: F(5,6) = 1800 is multiplied by the owner facing forward vector for the same origin calculation. The target defaults to owner location + one forward unit, or the secondary target’s actor location when valid.

6.label: Offset interval
6.simple: Controls the delay between effects inside one volley stage.
6.technical: F(6,6) = 0.02 is stored as ShotRequest.Interval. TickShotRequests subtracts delta time divided by a positive CustomTimeDilation (or 1.0 otherwise), fires the next offset once the timer reaches 0 or below, then resets the timer to Interval until all offsets in that stage are used.

7.label: Stage interval
7.simple: Controls the delay between volley stages.
7.technical: F(7,6) = 0.05 is stored as ShotRequest.StageInterval. When a stage’s offsets are exhausted, Stage advances, SubIndex resets and the timer becomes this value; the request is removed once Stage reaches StageCount.

8.label: Volley offset scale
8.simple: Scales the spacing of the effect offsets.
8.technical: F(8,6) = 0.6 is stored as ShotRequest.Scale. TickShotRequests multiplies each static offset translation by this scalar before composing it with the request transform; rotation and the base request transform are not scaled.

9.label: Target lead factor
9.simple: Extends the shikigami’s simulated flight time for a moving target.
9.technical: When the down/blown condition is true and the ahead trace is clear, Lead = F(9,6) * (distance from spawn origin to target * 0.001). That lead is added to the remaining distance as Lead * target horizontal speed and is also added to the simulated flight Time used to lead the target’s vertical fall; greater stored values increase both terms.

notes.text: A ShotRequest starts with Timer = -1.0f, so the first volley effect fires on the first action tick that sees the timer at or below zero.
StageCount is not in this row: controller CursedEnergyLevel maps 1 to 1 stage, 2 to 2 stages and 3 or 4 to 3 stages.
The dynamic index used for CP_120_ATTACKG_1_n / _2_n selects AttackSetDataTables rows by cursed-energy level and left-stick direction; it is not a unique-row index. The unique row stays 6.
Verification notes describe the same target-aware shikigami 3 trajectory and two line traces; the source transcription is the source of the exact formulas above.

CP_120_ATTACKH.title: CursedEnergyAttack_2 shikigami placement
CP_120_ATTACKH.overview: Row 7 positions shikigami 2 for all four CursedEnergyAttack_2 variants before the shared start/reset and summon behavior runs.

0.label: Forward summon offset
0.simple: Sets how far in front of Geto shikigami 2 appears.
0.technical: On the first start with a pending summon, F(0,7) = 118 becomes the X component of the shikigami SummonOffset vector and is also multiplied by the owner facing forward vector for FindSummonLocation. The vector’s Z is explicitly 0; the summon height itself comes from the shikigami’s FollowHeightOffset.

1.label: Right summon offset
1.simple: Sets how far to Geto’s right shikigami 2 appears.
1.technical: F(1,7) = 10 becomes the Y component of SummonOffset and is multiplied by the owner right vector in the same world-offset calculation. The placement result is passed to RequestLocation with priority 3.

notes.text: The row is shared by normal, air, auto and air-auto CursedEnergyAttack_2. Auto variants send Attack_2 and mark +0xA2; the other two send Attack_1.
For a player-controlled Geto, the +0x449 camera-bounds-test flag is cleared after the summon; that flag is not sourced from this row.
The start and reset bodies are CP_030-shared, while the finish effect is the generic AttackBase finisher plus shikigami release handling; none of those shared bodies adds another read of row 7.

The six shikigami indices have different roles in this controller: 0 and 1 are the normal-attack pair, 2 is the cursed-energy-2 summon, 3 is the cursed-energy-1 trajectories summon, 4 is the 1_1 summon and 5 is the 3_1 summon.

Cursed-energy staging is a controller/action-state mechanic, not a unique-float value: the base normal-attack tick stages CursedEnergyAttack_1 and _2 while staging is active, and notify parameters 20/30 arm it at level 2/3.

Some action bodies are deliberately shared with other character codes (CP_030 start/reset, CP_060 request removal, generic NormalAttack_3 bodies). Unlisted action types are delegated to UGameCharacterActionController::CreateAction; none of those shared paths was found to add another CP_120 unique-float read.

The CP_120 AI think node is distinct from a CP_120 behavior controller: it enables advanced behavior and weights several normal attacks, and setup group 211 uses fixed AI conditions rather than unique floats.
CP_120_ATTACKC_02_01 in CN_050 code is a DamageDataTables row used by the shikigami character CN_050, not this unique row C; row-name prefixes can be reused across tables.

The raw accessor is unchecked: GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue dereferences UniqueRows[RowIndex] and FloatValue[ValueIndex] directly. The verification note records that the retail body matches this raw dereference.
The CP_120 effect spawner queues fade effects with FX_CP_120_00133, but its inputs are effect IDs and transforms; no trap or MakeUniqueCameraRequest forwarding from CP_120 was found.
